name: An experiment roadmap
description: the dependency graph of an experiment's bench sessions: each step, which steps it waits on, the time window it must fall in after them, and which steps are parks where the work can stop indefinitely; the gantt-like plan a calendar is filled from one flight at a time
phrases: the shape of an experiment roadmap
which bench steps depend on which
time window between restreak and pick
where can this experiment be paused

id.description: short name; the file name where the roadmap is kept

name.description: the GOAL: what finishing the steps makes possible. It is not a step and is never performed.

source.description: what produced it: `c6-plan --roadmap`, or by hand

derived_from.description: the construction and characterization files it was planned from

title.description: what a person does, as a todo would say it

after.description: the steps this one waits on; direct predecessors only

operation.description: the labsheet operation, when derived from a plan

module.description: the protocol module the step is run from

work_min.description: hands-on minutes. ABSENT means unmeasured, never zero.

window.description: when this step must be done, in hours after its latest predecessor was done; from the predecessor protocol's `next` (protocols/TIMING.txt). A step with a window is part of a flight.

park.description: nothing after this step is on a clock; a flight ends here

timing.description: the protocol carries no timing data, so the step is unmeasured

progress.description: per step id: `{state, at, why?}`, state one of not-started | enabled | in-flight | done | failed. Kept by whoever runs the experiment, not by C6.

notes: Produced by `c6-plan <files> --roadmap <id> --goal "..."`, one step per labsheet. C6 answers what the steps are and under what windows; deciding WHEN is the scheduler's (Cortex spec/runtime.md section 25), and C6 never reads a calendar. A step whose protocol has no timing is emitted with `timing: unknown` rather than a guessed number, so a placer treats it as unmeasured. Windows come only from `next` on the protocol module; a protocol with neither `next` nor `park` hands its successor no window, which reads as 'not time-forced', so filling in `next` for the remaining modules is what makes more flights visible.
